annotation.title_clean: Women, ethics, robots, AI and data (WERAID) – How can we build the politics of love as we create new technologies?
annotation.title_en: Women, ethics, robots, AI and data (WERAID) – How can we build the politics of love as we create new technologies?
annotation.venue: ICRES 2022: 7th International Conference on Robot Ethics and Standards, Seoul
annotation.summary_en: Abstract of a keynote talk at ICRES 2022 by Kathleen Richardson introducing 'representational technologies of the human' (robots and AI mimicking human bodies and relationships), questioning whether relational, sexual and therapeutic roles should be delegated to machines, and proposing technology ethics informed by a politics of love.
key_provisions_or_claims: Introduces 'representational technologies of the human' (RTH) as a mimesis-based concept.
Asks what making sex/companion robots reveals about conceptions of women, men and children.
Questions whether relational, sexual and therapeutic roles should be outsourced to machines.
Proposes a new set of technology ideas informed by the politics of love.
